issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping and failure
issues.sym: Slipping, harsh or delayed shifts, flaring between gears, shudder in overdrive, or a sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in these cars has a long record of internal wear, torque converter trouble and outright failure, usually at higher mileage. The 2002-2005 cars draw the most reports.
issues.next: Have fluid condition and codes checked at the first sign of slipping and avoid hard driving until then. A unit that slips or loses drive usually needs a rebuild or replacement before it strands you.

issues.t: Car may roll away in Park (recall)
issues.sym: The car moves or creeps after you shift into Park, or Park does not feel like it locks.
issues.why: Several 1996-1997 recalls covered parts of the park mechanism in the transmission, including the park pawl shaft, its roll pin and an abutment bracket, which could keep the pawl from engaging.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Always set the parking brake, and get the car checked right away if it ever moves in Park.

issues.t: Transmission servo cover can leak fluid (recall)
issues.sym: Red fluid under the car, low transmission fluid, then slipping or delayed shifts.
issues.why: A servo cover on the AX4S automatic can come loose and leak transmission fluid. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and check the transmission fluid level. Do not keep driving with low fluid, which can ruin the transmission.

issues.t: Front seat belt buckle stud can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no symptom; the buckle may feel loose where it mounts to the seat.
issues.why: The stud that anchors the front seat belt buckle can crack, which could let the belt fail in a crash. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the buckle inspected.

issues.t: Engine may not return to idle (recall)
issues.sym: The engine keeps revving after you lift off the gas pedal, so the car does not slow down as expected.
issues.why: A clip on the accelerator cable can come off and let the throttle stick open. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the engine does not drop to idle, shift to neutral, brake to a safe stop and have it towed.

issues.t: Broken coil springs that can cut a tire
issues.sym: A loud bang or clunk, the car sitting lower at one corner, or a front tire suddenly going flat or shredded.
issues.why: Coil springs on these cars can rust and snap, and a broken end can slice into the tire. Ford recalled 1999-2001 front springs in salt-belt states; 2002-2003 cars were investigated by the government without a recall.
issues.next: Look at the springs during tire rotations, especially in salt-belt states, and check your VIN for the recall. Replace broken springs right away and inspect the tire next to them before driving further.

issues.t: Adjustable pedals set too close together (recall)
issues.sym: Your foot can catch the gas pedal while pressing the brake, making the car speed up unexpectedly.
issues.why: On cars with power adjustable pedals, the brake and gas pedals can end up too close together. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have it done before regular driving. Wear narrow shoes until it is fixed.

issues.t: Brake lights may not work right (recall)
issues.sym: Brake lights stay off when braking, stay on when you are not braking, or the cruise control acts up.
issues.why: The brake light switch or its wiring can malfunction, and grease from the pedals could get into the switch. Ford ran recalls on both problems.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have someone confirm your brake lights work. Faulty brake lights raise the risk of being rear-ended.

issues.t: Windshield wipers can stop working (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers slow down, stop part way, or quit entirely.
issues.why: A switch in the wiper motor gear case can overheat, and the wipers can stop working. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Do not drive in rain or snow if the wipers act up.

issues.t: Air filter can smolder or burn (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell or smoke from the engine bay.
issues.why: The paper in some air filters could catch fire. Ford recalled affected cars to replace the filter.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you see smoke or smell burning from under the hood, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Power seat support weld may be weak (recall)
issues.sym: The power seat feels loose, rocks, or creaks.
issues.why: A weld in the upper support of the power seat may not have been made properly. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the seat inspected, since a loose seat is a crash risk.

issues.t: Wiper motor can fail from missing grease (recall)
issues.sym: The wipers make grinding noises, slow down, or stop working.
issues.why: Some wiper motors were built without enough grease and the gears can fail. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Do not drive in bad weather if the wipers are failing.

issues.t: Inside door handle spring can unseat (recall)
issues.sym: The inside door handle feels loose or does not snap back after you pull it.
issues.why: The return spring for the interior door handle can come out of place, which could let the door unlatch in a side crash. Ford recalled cars built from late 2009 to mid 2010.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the handles repaired.

issues.t: License plate light can short and cause a fire (recall)
issues.sym: The license plate light flickers or quits, or you notice a burning smell near the trunk lid.
issues.why: Road salt can corrode the license plate lamp and its wiring and cause a short circuit that could start a fire. Ford recalled cars in salt-belt states.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you smell burning at the back of the car, stop driving it and have it inspected.

issues.t: Electric power steering can shut off (recall)
issues.sym: A steering warning message appears and the steering suddenly becomes very heavy.
issues.why: The electric power steering system can detect a fault and switch off the assist. Ford recalled affected cars, and steering problems are the top owner complaint for these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If assist cuts out, slow down, steer firmly to a safe stop and have the car checked before driving on.

issues.t: Fuel tank seam can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell or wet spots under the fuel tank.
issues.why: A side seam on the fuel tank may not be fully sealed and can leak. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you smell fuel, do not drive the car until it is inspected.

issues.t: Fuel pump module can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A fuel smell, especially after filling up, or fuel dripping near the tank.
issues.why: The fuel delivery module on top of the tank can crack and leak fuel. Ford ran two recalls on this part.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. Do not drive the car if you smell fuel; leaking fuel is a fire risk.

issues.t: Rear child safety locks can switch off (recall)
issues.sym: The rear doors open from inside even though the child locks are set.
issues.why: The child safety locks on some early-built cars can turn themselves off. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and test the child locks before carrying children in back.

issues.t: Fuel pump can lose power and stall the EcoBoost engine (recall)
issues.sym: Hard starting, stumbling, or the engine stalling, sometimes without warning.
issues.why: A part inside the fuel pump module can overheat and cut power to the pump. Ford recalled SHO and police cars with the 3.5L EcoBoost engine.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and get the repair done promptly, since a stall at speed is dangerous.

issues.t: Axle can come apart from the linkshaft (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking from under the car, then sudden loss of drive.
issues.why: The halfshaft can disengage from the linkshaft while driving, leaving the car without power and possibly unable to hold in Park. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you lose drive, stop safely, set the parking brake and have the car towed.

issues.t: Axle support bracket can fail (recall)
issues.sym: Clunking or vibration from the front, then loss of drive, or the car rolling in Park.
issues.why: The halfshaft support bracket can break, which can cause a loss of power or loss of the Park function. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Always use the parking brake, and have the car towed if you lose drive.

issues.t: Rear toe link can break (recall, SHO and police)
issues.sym: Clunking from the rear, the car wandering, or a sudden change in handling.
issues.why: The rear suspension toe link on SHO and Police Interceptor cars can fracture, which affects steering control. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If the rear feels loose or the car pulls oddly, slow down and have it inspected before driving further.

issues.t: Fuel tank bolts may be loose (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or clunking from under the rear of the car, or a fuel smell.
issues.why: Fuel tank attachment bolts may not have been tightened properly, so the tank could come loose. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the tank mounting checked before regular driving.

issues.t: Parking brake may not fully apply (recall)
issues.sym: The car rolls slightly with the parking brake set, especially on a hill.
issues.why: The parking brake may not engage fully on affected cars. Ford recalled them for repair.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Park in gear and on level ground where possible until it is fixed.

issues.t: Turbo oil lines can leak (recall)
issues.sym: An oil smell, smoke from the engine bay, or oil spots under the car.
issues.why: The oil supply tubes for the turbochargers on the 3.5L EcoBoost can leak oil onto hot parts. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. If you see smoke or smell burning oil, pull over and stop the engine.

issues.t: Backup camera picture can be blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: The rearview camera shows a distorted, blank or on-and-off picture when you back up.
issues.why: Ford recalled 2015-2016 and 2018-2019 Taurus models for a rearview camera image problem.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall (2017 models are not listed). Back up using mirrors until it is fixed.

issues.t: Door pillar trim can come off while driving (recall)
issues.sym: Rattling or wind noise from the front door pillar, or the trim panel loosening.
issues.why: The driver and passenger B-pillar trim pieces can detach while driving and become a hazard to other drivers. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have loose trim secured.

issues.t: Steering gear heat shield can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: A rattle from under the front of the car.
issues.why: Fasteners holding the steering gear heat shield can corrode and let the shield fall off. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall and have the shield secured at your next service.

issues.t: Key can come out when not in Park (recall)
issues.sym: You can remove the key with the shifter not fully in Park, and the car may roll away.
issues.why: On cars with a turn-key ignition, the key could be removed without the transmission in Park. Ford recalled affected cars.
issues.next: Check your VIN for an open recall. Always confirm the car is in Park and set the parking brake before getting out.

issues.t: Internal water pump leaks and can put coolant in the oil
issues.sym: Coolant level that keeps dropping, drips or a puddle near the passenger side of the engine, overheating, or milky-looking oil on the dipstick.
issues.why: The water pump sits inside the engine behind the timing cover and is driven by the timing chain. When its seal wears, coolant can leak outside or drain into the oil pan, which ruins the bearings if the engine keeps running.
issues.next: If coolant is disappearing or the oil looks milky, stop driving and have it inspected. Replacing the pump is a big job, and shops usually renew the timing chain parts at the same time.

issues.t: Six-speed automatic shifts roughly or hesitates
issues.sym: A clunk or flare between gears, a pause before the car moves off, slipping under light throttle, and sometimes a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners of the first years of this six-speed report shift quality going off as miles build up, from the valve body and its solenoids or the control software rather than one broken part.
issues.next: Have the fluid level and condition checked and the codes read early. A fluid service or valve body work is far cheaper than waiting for the transmission to fail.

issues.t: Clicking from the heater blend door actuator
issues.sym: A fast clicking, ticking or ratcheting sound comes from behind the dash, often right after startup or when you change the temperature. One side may blow the wrong temperature.
issues.why: The small electric motor that moves the blend door inside the heater box strips its plastic gear teeth, so it keeps hunting for a position it can no longer reach.
issues.next: Not urgent. The actuator has to be replaced to stop the noise and get even temperature control back.
